scenes.name: The Town of Ekacakrā
scenes.display: After the burning of the lac house, the five Pāṇḍava brothers lived hidden in the town of Ekacakrā, disguised as brahmins, begging their bread. But over that town hung a shadow.

scenes.name: The Demon's Toll
scenes.display: In the wood lived Bakāsura, a rākṣasa who devoured men. Each week the town sent him a cartload of food — and the one who drove the cart. Now the lot fell on the very house that had sheltered them; and the brahmin's family wept.

scenes.name: Kuntī's Word
scenes.display: Then Kuntī said quietly: "Do not grieve. You gave my sons shelter; my son shall take your place." And she chose Bhīma — the strongest of the five.

scenes.name: The Cart of Food
scenes.display: At dawn Bhīma drove the loaded cart toward the forest — and being Bhīma, and being hungry, he ate the demon's dinner himself along the way.

scenes.name: Baka Falls
scenes.display: The rākṣasa came roaring from the trees — huge as a hill, furious at the empty cart. They fought, tree against fist, until Bhīma seized him and broke his back across his knee.

scenes.name: The Town Set Free
scenes.display: In the morning the people of Ekacakrā found the demon dead at their gates, and wondered who had saved them. The brahmins kept their secret — and walked on quietly, toward Pāñcāla, and a destiny that would change the world.
